title: The default vwf gate lines examine every file (--all)

keeps.check: No default gate line in plugins/vwf/ or in this repo's CONTRIBUTING.md runs code:format or code:lint without --all: command grep -rnE 'mise run code:(format|lint)' plugins/vwf CONTRIBUTING.md
keeps.pass: Each hit has --all as a flag of the code:format or code:lint command, before any redirect or comment; or is one of exactly two bare daily lines (mise run code:format and mise run code:lint) in each file that holds the daily-checks block (D6, D19, D18); or is prose that names the task and no command line. The run report lists each allowed hit with its reason.

release_levels.reason: The default unit and wave gate lines that the two planners propose take --all, so a gate on a clean worktree examines every file after bootstrap 4.0.0.
The manual names the new default gate lines.

shared_files.why: every human-facing doc belongs to the docs unit

decisions.decision: Which default gate lines take --all?
decisions.ruling: The default unit gate is mise x -- mise run code:format --all, and the default wave gate is mise x -- mise run code:lint --all. After bootstrap 4.0.0, code:format and code:lint examine only the uncommitted files when they get no files and no --all. The wave gate runs before wave 1 and after the units commit, on a clean worktree, so without --all it examines nothing.
decisions.rejected: Keep the unit gate without --all, because it runs before the commit of a unit, when its files are uncommitted. The bootstrap prompt asks for both lines with --all, and one rule for both lines is clearer.

decisions.decision: Does the default plan gate change?
decisions.ruling: No. The plan gate stays mise x -- mise run code:precommit. It always runs pre-commit with --all-files and takes no flag.
decisions.rejected: Add --all to code:precommit.

decisions.decision: Does /vwf:execute get new logic?
decisions.ruling: No. /vwf:execute runs the gate lines that the folder records and nothing it infers, so a change to the default lines is enough. Only the example line of execute/references/action-log.md changes, to the new wave gate line.
decisions.rejected: A preflight check in /vwf:execute that refuses a code:format or code:lint gate line without --all.

decisions.decision: Do the queued plans change their gate lines?
decisions.ruling: No. The plans that are already queued keep their gate lines (bootstrap gap 2026-11-15-vwf-gates-all-parked, D55 of its plan). Their gates still pass, but examine fewer files. No unit edits a folder under docs/plans/.
decisions.rejected: Rewrite the gate lines of each queued folder.

decisions.decision: When can this plan run?
decisions.ruling: Amended 2026-11-18 (D23): requires nothing. The first ruling required docs/plans/2026-11-14-git-over-tasks (R3b), because this repo then ran bootstrap 3.3.1 tasks that fail on --all. On 2026-11-18 this repo moved to bootstrap 4.1.1 (commit df7ea322), its code:format and code:lint declare #USAGE flag --all, and R3a is COMPLETE, so this plan and its own gate lines can run now.
decisions.rejected: requires R3a (its COMPLETE state does not prove that the D15 hand step ran); no requires (plans written here before the bootstrap init get gate lines that fail).

decisions.decision: What happens to the two daily commands of the hygiene asset CONTRIBUTING.md?
decisions.ruling: Keep mise run code:format and mise run code:lint as the daily commands. Correct their comments to say that they examine the uncommitted files (staged, changed and new). Add one line each that shows the same command with --all, with a comment that says it examines every file of the repository.
decisions.rejected: Add --all to the two daily commands (slower for each contributor); leave the lines as they are (the comment 'every formatter, over what it owns' becomes false).

decisions.decision: Do the stackgen pack texts that name mise run code:lint or code:format change?
decisions.ruling: No. They say which tool a task runs, for example that mise run code:lint runs ktlint, and that stays true. No unit touches plugins/stackgen/.
decisions.rejected: Add --all to each pack text.

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: No. The plan changes prose only and lands no runnable code, so the wave review is the only review.
decisions.rejected: One review unit after U1.

decisions.decision: Which execution mode?
decisions.ruling: solo. Each wave has one edit unit, so no unit has a peer to send a message to.
decisions.rejected: teams.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 1 gap 1: in a target repo whose code:format and code:lint are older than bootstrap 4.0.0, a gate line with --all passes --all as a file and fails. What do the planners propose there?
decisions.ruling: Always propose --all when mise tasks ls --hidden lists code:format and code:lint. This case is accepted: after R3a, vwf supports only a repo on the bootstrap 4.0.0 contract, and /vwf:doctor reports an old-form repo as blocking (R3a D26).
decisions.rejected: Propose --all only when the task declares #USAGE flag "--all", else the bare line; always --all with a note at the gate.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 1 gap 2: the --all lines that D6 adds to the hygiene asset CONTRIBUTING.md fail in a target repo whose tasks are older than bootstrap 4.0.0. Does the asset show them?
decisions.ruling: Yes. This case is accepted for the same reason as D10: after R3a, /vwf:init adopts bootstrap 4.0.0, so a repo that gets the asset has the new tasks.
decisions.rejected: Correct only the two comments and show no --all line.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 1 gap 3: /vwf:init writes a hygiene asset only when the repo does not have it (init/references/readme-and-license.md:30-31). A repo that already holds CONTRIBUTING.md keeps the comment every formatter, over what it owns. Does this plan update it?
decisions.ruling: No. This case is accepted and out of scope. The file belongs to each repo after init writes it, and its commands still run; only one comment is less exact.
decisions.rejected: Park a gap record for an update path of present hygiene assets; a /vwf:doctor row that reports the old comment.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2 gap 1: R3b U3 adds a one-branch variant of the hygiene CONTRIBUTING file beside CONTRIBUTING.md, with the same daily-checks block, under a name it does not fix. Does U1 edit it?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U1 owns plugins/vwf/skills/init/assets/hygiene/CONTRIBUTING*.md and applies the D6 edit to the daily-checks block of each file that matches.
decisions.rejected: U1 edits only CONTRIBUTING.md, and the variant keeps the old comments.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2 gap 2: the sentence above the daily-checks block of the hygiene CONTRIBUTING files says there is nothing to remember beyond running them before you push. After a commit, the bare code:format and code:lint examine nothing. Does U1 change it?
decisions.ruling: Yes. In each CONTRIBUTING*.md, U1 rewrites that sentence: while you work, the bare commands examine the uncommitted files; before you push, run the --all forms, which examine every file of the repository. This widens D6 by this one sentence.
decisions.rejected: Change only the sh block and leave the sentence.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2 gap 3: K1 passed only when each hit ends in --all, but the action-log example ends in a redirect and the CONTRIBUTING lines end in a comment.
decisions.ruling: K1 passes when each hit has --all as a flag of the command, before any redirect or comment. The planner corrected the wording; it has one correct answer.
decisions.rejected: Keep ends in --all.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2 gap 4: CLAUDE.md (about line 243) says the lint hook calls code:lint, which runs the house linter over the whole tree. With the 4.0.0 tasks, the hook passes the staged files and only --all examines the whole tree. Does U2 correct it?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U2 rewrites that clause: the lint hook calls code:lint with the staged files, and code:lint --all lints the whole tree, so every linter exclusion still lives in .config/linter.yaml and nowhere else. .claude/docs/repo-shape.md (about lines 122-125) already says the hooks pass the staged files, and stays.
decisions.rejected: Leave CLAUDE.md as it is.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2 gap 5: the queued plan docs/plans/2026-11-15-config-format-28 (R4b, priority 60) also edits plugins/vwf/skills/change-plan/references/gates-consent.md, and this plan does not order itself against it.
decisions.ruling: Accepted. Priority 40 puts this plan before R4b, and R4b edits a different passage of the file, so its run starts from this plan text. No requires is added.
decisions.rejected: Add docs/plans/2026-11-15-config-format-28 to requires (priority 70).

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 3 gap 1: this repo own CONTRIBUTING.md (about lines 50-55) says nothing to remember beyond running them before you push, and that code:format runs the formatter, over what it owns. Both become false with the 4.0.0 tasks. Does a unit own it?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U2 owns CONTRIBUTING.md and applies the D6 and D14 edits to its gates section: the comments of the two bare daily commands say that they examine the uncommitted files; one --all line each is added; the sentence above the block names the --all forms as the pre-push form.
decisions.rejected: Leave this repo CONTRIBUTING.md as it is.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 3 gap 2: R3b does not fix the name or folder of its one-branch CONTRIBUTING variant, so a CONTRIBUTING*.md glob can miss it.
decisions.ruling: U1 owns plugins/vwf/skills/init/assets/hygiene/** and applies the D6 and D14 edits to each file there that holds the daily-checks block of mise run code:format and mise run code:lint, found by content. If only CONTRIBUTING.md holds it, U1 edits that one file and reports so in a DECIDED line. This replaces the glob of D13.
decisions.rejected: Keep the CONTRIBUTING*.md glob, and return a QUESTION when no second file matches.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 3 gap 3: this plan and 2026-11-14-virajp-plugins-tool (R3c) both have priority 40. Which runs first?
decisions.ruling: The row gets priority 40 (10 + 30 of R3b). plan.mjs pick breaks a tie by the date of the folder name (plan-management/scripts/lib/queue.mjs, about lines 390-393), so R3c (2026-11-14) runs first and this plan next. D17 holds. The planner recorded this fact; it has one answer.
decisions.rejected: none

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 3 gap 4: must K1 and the U1 grep accept exactly two bare daily lines per file, and does init/references/readme-and-license.md (about line 36) change?
decisions.ruling: K1 accepts exactly two bare daily lines in each file that holds the daily-checks block. readme-and-license.md only names the gate tasks, so it stays correct and no unit edits it. The planner recorded this; it has one answer.
decisions.rejected: none

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 4 gap 1: the new --all lines are longer than the comment column of the daily-checks sh block, so aligned comments need a new column on every line of the block, against Change nothing else.
decisions.ruling: U1 and U2 move the comment column of the whole daily-checks sh block, so that all comments align. On the lines they do not otherwise change (code:sec, code:precommit), only whitespace changes.
decisions.rejected: Keep the other lines and accept misaligned comments.

decisions.decision: After approval, this repo moved to bootstrap 4.1.1 (commit df7ea322, ops: migrate to bootstrap v4), and R3a became COMPLETE. The reason of D5 for requires R3b is gone. Does the plan keep requires R3b?
decisions.ruling: No. requires becomes [], and the row priority becomes 10. D20 (the tie at 40 with R3c) no longer applies; D17 still holds, because this plan now runs before R4b too.
decisions.rejected: Keep requires R3b and priority 40.
